stdout:
[
  {
    "id": "houserules.pnpm-only",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Use pnpm for every package operation in this repository (`pnpm install`, `pnpm add --save-exact`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm dlx`); never `npm` or `npx`."
  },
  {
    "id": "houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Treat `~/projects/tag-pilot` as a read-only reference: never modify it, commit there, run its agents, or run `init` or `update` against it."
  },
  {
    "id": "houserules.template-is-the-source",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Edit the kit in `template/`, then run `node bin/houserules.mjs update --dir .`; never hand-edit the root copies or the generated rules and skill."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.ask-when-missing",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Ask the user when information is missing. Do not assume."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.backlog-drives-work",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "The backlog drives all work. Select backlog items before you start; every requirement traces to an item."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.brainstorm-first",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Start each batch with a brainstorming session or a written spec; get the user's approval before implementing."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.code-health-scan",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Every plan carries a code-health scan of the files the batch touches: name the smells and antipatterns found, and fold targeted fixes into the tasks."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.conventional-commits",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Commits use Conventional Commits (feat, fix, chore, test, ci, docs, refactor). Header at most 100 characters, body lines at most 100."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.deliverables-json",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Task reports, reviews, and branch reviews are JSON files that pass `tools/kb.sh validate` against `.claude/schemas/deliverables.json`."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.ff-only-merges",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Merge fast-forward only, from the CLI, after aggregating the branch into clean logical commits. No merge commits, no GitHub squash merges."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.knowledge-first",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Before you change a file, read its knowledge: the ids in your task and `tools/kb.sh for <path>`. Cite the ids you relied on in your report."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.live-run-before-ci",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Verify a change live (run the app, service, or tool for real; capture evidence) before any PR, merge, or deploy spend."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.model-policy",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Every review runs on a mightier model than the implementer it reviews. Implementers use the cheapest model that fits the task."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.no-tech-debt",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Fix every review finding, Minor included. Defer a fix only for a stated reason, as a backlog item; never as a TODO in code."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.rulings-to-file",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Every ruling goes to its home file in the same turn — a deferral’s backlog item included. A ledger and the chat are not home files; neither survives compaction."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.sequential-agents",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Run all agent work strictly sequentially. Never dispatch two implementers or two reviewers at the same time."
  },
  {
    "id": "process.tdd",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "process",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Test-driven development for every executable change: the failing test first, or a disclosed-mutation proof for already-correct behavior; verbatim RED and GREEN."
  },
  {
    "id": "quality.no-compat-softening",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Never soften a design for backward compatibility. Make the correct change and migrate everything it breaks; the codebase is not built on compromises."
  },
  {
    "id": "quality.principles",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "YAGNI, KISS, DRY; prefer a well-maintained library to custom code; one responsibility per unit; tests assert behavior; a11y and i18n are part of done."
  },
  {
    "id": "security-hygiene.dependency-vetting",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Verify every new dependency is well-maintained before adding it. Record the check in the task report's `dependency_vetting` field."
  },
  {
    "id": "security-hygiene.exact-pins",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Pin exact versions. Install only with a CLI (`pnpm add --save-exact`, `cargo add <crate>@=<version>`). Never write a version number by hand."
  },
  {
    "id": "security-hygiene.no-coauthor",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Never add a co-author or session trailer line to any commit."
  },
  {
    "id": "security-hygiene.no-focused-tests",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Never commit a focused test (`.only(`)."
  },
  {
    "id": "security-hygiene.verify-current-docs",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Verify every library, tool, and framework API against current docs before use. Internal knowledge is stale."
  },
  {
    "id": "writing-style.code-comments",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Write a code comment only for a constraint the code cannot show."
  },
  {
    "id": "writing-style.doc-comments",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Document every exported symbol with the language's doc-comment convention. Name things so the code reads without comments."
  },
  {
    "id": "writing-style.principles",
    "kind": "rule",
    "area": "global",
    "standing": true,
    "summary": "Write docs, comments, commit messages, and reports in ASD-STE100 style: short sentences, active voice, one instruction per sentence, concise."
  }
]
